A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Uni-AD under the same title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAD-eval-Named generation results, component and pretraining ablations, contextual-information experiments, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains original MAD experiments and adds Uni-AD results on CMDAD and TVAD, character-refinement measurements, and a threshold ablation.

M1.justification: The core interleaved prompting, contextual modeling, and losses remain unchanged. For CMDAD/TVAD, v2 introduces a variant using VideoLLaMA visual mapping and AutoAD-Zero character inputs, with a one-block, 4096-channel character refiner instead of the MAD configuration's three-block, 768-channel refiner (Section 4.1, Table S1).

E1.justification: v2 adds CMDAD movie training/evaluation and TVAD television-series evaluation to the retained MAD coverage, substantially expanding the evaluated populations and domains. The WebVid2M pretraining study and dataset description present in v1 are removed.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds AutoAD-III and AutoAD-Zero to the existing MAD comparison, materially expanding the competitive evaluation. New Table 2 compares against AutoAD-II, AutoAD-III, and AutoAD-Zero on CMDAD, and against AutoAD-III and AutoAD-Zero on TVAD.

E3.justification: The added experiments train on CMDAD and evaluate on CMDAD and TVAD using dataset-specific visual and character configurations. Evaluation adds CRITIC character-name overlap and LLM-AD-eval using llama2-7b-chat (Appendix B.4). The previously reported batch sizes, learning rates, optimizer, and ten-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's dedicated partial-pretraining ablation, including harmful WebVid effects, is removed (Table 4). v2 adds a focused character-selection threshold study covering 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 (Table S6). The other component, contextual-information, and qualitative analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark results, including Uni-AD CIDEr scores of 21.8 on CMDAD and 26.6 on TVAD, plus threshold and character-refinement results. Distinct WebVid pretraining results disappear. In the matched MAD contextual row, ROUGE-L changes from 17.2 to 17.1 and R@5/16 from 54.9 to 54.2; CIDEr remains 28.2 (v1 Tables 1/5a; v2 Tables 1/5).

T1.justification: The prompt construction, contextual concatenation, contrastive loss, and autoregressive objective are mathematically unchanged. Equations are combined and renumbered. Descriptions of existing evaluation metrics add explanation, without new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The main methodological contributions remain the same. The introduction and conclusion broaden the performance claim from MAD to multiple AD benchmarks, while the abstract replaces its MAD state-of-the-art statement with the more qualified claim that Uni-AD performs well on multiple datasets.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that high character-selection thresholds discard useful character information. It removes v1's explanations for WebVid-related degradation and AutoAD-II's resistance to noisy character inputs. Existing limitations concerning imperfect character recognition and errors from predicted context ADs remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset-specific architecture, feature-extractor, character-bank, and LLM-judge details, and changes the code statement from a planned release to stated availability at a different repository. It removes the LoRA pretraining detail, Table 1's pretraining information, the BERTScore similarity specification, and GPU memory capacity. Core training hyperparameters remain documented.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion incorporates AutoAD-III's Q-former approach and AutoAD-Zero's training-free pipeline, with additional references supporting newer visual and language models. Frozen in Time/WebVid, LoRA, and BERTScore references disappear. The overall interleaved-prompting motivation and related-work organization remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits and condenses the abstract, introduction, and ablation discussion, converts contribution bullets into a paragraph, renames Section 3.2, and adds acknowledgements and an appendix overview heading. Most methodological prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout with extensive display restructuring. v1 Figures 3/4 merge into v2 Figure 3; Figure 6 splits into Figures S1/S2; Table 5 splits into Tables 5/6. The architecture table is reorganized, and benchmark, character-performance, and threshold tables are added.

improvement.justification: CMDAD/TVAD evaluation and CRITIC/LLM-AD-eval provide broader evidence about applicability, character accuracy, and description quality than v1's MAD-only evaluation. AutoAD-III/Zero comparisons and threshold analysis also strengthen assessment. These benefits are partly offset by losing informative pretraining failures and implementation details, plus incorrect ablation cross-references and the misleading Table S2 caption. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
